summary: WPA-built 1939 stone tower on Mount Penn, staffed until 1988, closed, then restored and reopened to the public in 2004.

facts.design: 120-ft stone tower with round copper-domed cab, 1939

access.note: Reopened to visitors in 2004; owned by the City of Reading, which does not own the surrounding fenced land.

visit.trail_note: On Skyline Drive on Mount Penn, about a mile from the Pagoda landmark.

events.note: Earlier wooden tower built on the site by the Mount Penn Gravity Railroad Company.
That wooden tower burned down, reportedly by arson.
Construction of the current stone tower began December 9, 1938, funded by a WPA grant plus city funds.
Tower completed in August 1939 and opened October 28, 1939.
Closed in September 1988 due to deterioration, ending its lookout/tourist use.
Added to the National Historic Lookout Register October 30, 1999.
Reopened to the public October 28, 2004 after restoration by a local nonprofit and Pagoda-Skyline, Inc.
The earlier wooden tower at this site registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites Register.

evidence.quote: Work on the structure began in late 1938 as a project of the Works Progress Administration (WPA), with the tower completed the following year.

evidence.supports: Reused foundation of 1889 tower burned in 1923
evidence.quote: The original tower operated from 1890 to 1923, when the wooden structure was destroyed in a purported act of arson.

evidence.supports: Architect studied other towers including Saint Paul, Minnesota
evidence.quote: He drew design inspiration for the tower by studying over half a dozen other fire lookout towers, including one from Saint Paul, Minnesota.
although deterioration to the building caused it to be closed in 1988
Starting in the late 1990s, a local nonprofit group began working to restore the tower, and it was reopened in 2004.

Built in 1939 by the City of Reading as a tourist attraction and fire observation post and staffed by the Pennsylvania Bureau of Forestry untill 1988... The City of Reading and Pagoda-Skyline, Inc. have restored the tower.

evidence.supports: Former wooden tower no longer standing, separately registered
evidence.quote: This wooden tower is no longer standing.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLOS lists a 'Mount Penn Tower Site' as a wooden tower no longer standing, but this refers to the pre-1939 wooden tower on the same site, not the current standing stone tower registered separately with NHLR.

notes_for_editor: FFLOS entry appears to document the earlier 1889 wooden tower on this site, not the current 1939 stone tower (which is NHLR-registered separately). Worth confirming if FFLOS and NHLR records are meant to be linked.
